Adverse events included development of new FTMHs in 5% of VMT-only eyes, and across all studies, retinal tears and detachments developed in 8 (1%) and 13 (2%) eyes, respectively.

Conclusion

Pneumatic vitreolysis appears to be a cost-effective treatment option for patients with vitreomacular traction without FTMH with modest to good success rates. Eyes with concurrent macular hole have a modest closure rate only. The risk of complications, including FTMH, retinal tear or detachment, must be considered.

records.title: Visual and refractive outcomes of laser vision correction in carefully selected patients with diabetes mellitus.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Visual and refractive outcomes of laser vision correction in carefully selected patients with diabetes mellitus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate real-world visual and refractive outcomes in the diabetes mellitus (DM) population. DM may impair corneal healing and neurosensory function, often serving as a relative contraindication for laser vision correction (LVC). This study evaluated visual and refractive outcomes of photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) and laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) in adults with controlled DM compared with healthy controls and compared the 2 techniques within the diabetic cohort.

Setting

Care Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel.

Design

Retrospective comparative study.

Methods

This retrospective study (2013 to 2024) included consecutive primary PRK or LASIK procedures in adults with controlled DM (hemoglobin A1c <8.0%, no worse than mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy, and no diabetic macular edema) and healthy controls. Eyes were propensity-matched on baseline characteristics. Outcomes included refractive and visual measures and complications (retreatment, dry eye, glare, infectious keratitis, haze, epithelial ingrowth, and diffuse lamellar keratitis).

Results

After matching, 784 myopic PRK eyes (158 DM), 471 myopic LASIK eyes (96 DM), 123 myopic DM eyes (86 PRK; 37 LASIK), and 611 hyperopic LASIK eyes (31 DM) were analyzed. Mean follow-up was approximately 3 to 5 months. Generalized estimating equations-adjusted analyses showed no significant differences in visual, refractive, or complication outcomes between DM and controls for myopic PRK or LASIK. Within the diabetic population, PRK and LASIK outcomes were comparable. Hyperopic LASIK outcomes were similar, although patients with DM showed a higher retreatment rate.

Conclusions

In carefully selected adults with controlled DM, both PRK and LASIK yielded comparable safety and visual outcomes with controls. These findings suggest LVC is viable for this population and that current guidelines may be overly conservative.

records.title: Long-Term Foveal Microvascular Alterations in Children With Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: An OCT Angiography Study.

content.title: Long-Term Foveal Microvascular Alterations in Children With Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: An OCT Angiography Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the foveal microvascular structure in children with a history of hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) compared with healthy controls.

Methods

This prospective cross-sectional comparative study included 46 eyes of 23 children with HIE and 40 eyes of 20 age-matched healthy controls. The children were grouped as follows: Group 1: HIE Stage I (n=28 eyes); Group 2: HIE Stage II-III (n=18 eyes); Group 3: healthy age-matched controls (n=40 eyes). Patients were also subgrouped based on fundus appearance within the first week of life as follows: Group A: eyes without any retinal hemorrhages (RHs) (n=13 eyes); Group B: eyes with widespread peripheral RHs sparing the macula (n=28 eyes); Group C: eyes with widespread peripheral RHs with macular involvement (n=5 eyes); Group D: healthy controls (n=40 eyes). All children underwent optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA)(Solix Visionix). FAZ area, foveal vessel densities and central foveal thickness (CFT) were compared.

Results

Foveal vessel density of the superficial capillary plexus (VD-SCP) and CFT were significantly higher in Group 2 compared with Group 1 (all p<0.05). Significantly smaller FAZ area was noted in Group 2 (0.19±0.09 mm2) compared with Group 1 (0.28±0.10 mm2) and 3 (0.26±0.09 mm2)(all p<0.05).

Conclusions

HIE may lead to persistent alterations in foveal microvasculature. OCTA may serve as a non-invasive biomarker for detecting long-term retinal microvascular sequelae in children with a history of perinatal asphyxia.

records.title: EVALUATION OF RETINAL AND CHOROIDAL CHANGES IN PATIENTS WITH CUSHING SYNDROME BEFORE AND AFTER ADRENALECTOMY USING WIDEFIELD SS-OCTA.

content.title: EVALUATION OF RETINAL AND CHOROIDAL CHANGES IN PATIENTS WITH CUSHING SYNDROME BEFORE AND AFTER ADRENALECTOMY USING WIDEFIELD SS-OCTA.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the structural and vascular alterations of central and peripheral retina/choroid in eyes of individuals with Cushing syndrome (CS) using widefield (24 × 20 mm 2 ) swept source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA), and explore the relationship between systemic factors and ocular indicators.

Methods

A total of 60 patients with CS (120 eyes) due to unilateral adrenal adenoma and 60 comparable healthy controls (HC, 120 eyes) were enrolled. Ocular parameters assessed using SS-OCTA included choroidal thickness (ChT) and choroidal vascularity index (CVI) as primary outcomes, while choroidal vessel/stromal volume per unit area (CVV/a, CSV/a), retinal thickness (RT), and retinal deep capillary plexus vessel density (DCPVD) were considered as secondary outcomes. SS-OCTA images were divided into 3 × 3 grid, with its grid center as central area and the rest as peripheral area. Cortisol levels were analyzed for correlations with choroidal parameters.

Results

Compared with HC, patients with CS exhibited increased ChT, CVI, CVV/a, CSV/a, and DCPVD ( P < 0.05). After adrenalectomy, decreased cortisol levels were accompanied with reduced ChT, CVI, CVV/a, and CSV/a ( P < 0.05), while no change was found in DCPVD. After controlling confounding factors, both SFCT and mean peripheral ChT were significantly correlated with 24-hour urine-free cortisol and 8 am cortisol ( P < 0.05).

Conclusion

Patients with CS demonstrate abnormal choroidal thickness and volume. Further correlation analysis show choroidal thickness is positively related to endogenous cortisol levels, suggesting potential links between cortisol and ocular health.

records.title: MIDPHASE HYPERFLUORESCENT PLAQUES AS A BIOMARKER OF DISEASE ACTIVITY IN CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: Clinical Course and Treatment Response - MICRoN Report Number Ten.

content.title: MIDPHASE HYPERFLUORESCENT PLAQUES AS A BIOMARKER OF DISEASE ACTIVITY IN CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: Clinical Course and Treatment Response - MICRoN Report Number Ten.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate the association between midphase hyperfluorescent plaques (MPHP) with subretinal fluid (SRF) dynamics in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) and to assess response across different therapeutic modalities using a validated quantitative approach.

Methods

This was a retrospective, multicenter study in patients with CSCR. All patients underwent baseline and follow-up indocyanine green angiography and enhanced depth imaging optical coherence tomography. MPHP were measured on midphase indocyanine green angiography images, and changes in MPHP number and area were correlated with various imaging parameters. Response of MPHP to different treatment modalities were also evaluated.

Results

The study included 96 eyes of 60 patients, 50 men (83.33%) and 10 women (16.67%) with CSCR. Over a median follow-up of 31 months, significant reductions were observed in central macular thickness ( P = 0.003), SRF height ( P = 0.02), subfoveal choroidal thickness ( P = 0.001), and MPHP area ( P = 0.02), while MPHP number and best recorded visual acuity remained stable. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) and laser induced greater SRF reduction (-125.0 ± 143.2 µ m and -123.8 ± 139.5 µ m) and MPHP area decrease (-4.14 ± 6.13 mm 2 and -1.75 ± 2.98 mm 2 , respectively) compared with Eplerenone and observation ( P < 0.01). Multivariable analysis confirmed PDT as the strongest independent predictor of MPHP area regression ( P ≤ 0.001), while baseline SRF height and symptom duration predicted final SRF height ( P ≤ 0.02).

Conclusion

MPHP represent a frequent and dynamic angiographic feature in CSCR, closely associated with disease activity. PDT significantly reduced MPHP area and promoted SRF resolution, supporting its role as an effective treatment.

records.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Course Prediction in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Using Baseline OCT from a Multicenter Cohort.

content.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Course Prediction in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Using Baseline OCT from a Multicenter Cohort.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To predict disease clinical course in central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC) using an interpretable machine learning model applied to baseline artificial intelligence (AI)-derived optical coherence tomography (OCT) biomarkers acquired at first presentation.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective cohort study.

Participants

Overall, 329 treatment-naïve CSC eyes recruited across eight international centers in Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and North Africa.

Methods

Treatment-naïve CSC patients were retrospectively included and classified, based on follow-up, as acute or chronic CSC according to subretinal fluid (SRF) resolution. Baseline OCT biomarkers were extracted using an AI-based platform (Discovery OCT Biomarker Detector; RetinAI AG, Switzerland), which quantified retinal layer thicknesses, including the outer nuclear layer (ONL) and photoreceptor-retinal pigment epithelium (PR+RPE) complex, fluid volumes (SRF and RPE detachment [PED]), and biomarker probabilities, across central, parafoveal, and perifoveal ETDRS regions. These features used to develop an interpretable machine learning model predicting future CSC chronicity.

Main outcome measures

Classification of eyes as acute or chronic CSC, determined by SRF resolution on follow-up; discriminative performance of the Random Forest classifier, assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); and biomarker importance, evaluated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values.

Results

Of 329 eyes (291 patients), 92 (28.0%) were classified as acute and 237 (72.0%) as chronic CSC; mean follow-up was 4.2 ± 1.6 years. Chronic CSC patients were significantly older (51.7 ± 12.6 vs. 43.2 ± 9.6 years, p<0.001) with worse baseline visual acuity (0.25 ± 0.21 vs. 0.16 ± 0.15 logMAR, p=0.029). Among baseline OCT biomarkers, parafoveal ONL thickness showed the strongest association with disease chronicity (q<0.0001; r=-0.414). The Random Forest classifier achieved an AUC of 0.852 (95% CI: 0.748-0.940). SHAP analysis identified parafoveal ONL thickness, perifoveal PR+RPE thickness, and central SRF volume as the strongest predictors of acute CSC, whereas greater RNFL thickness, PED volume, FLAT PED probability, and HF probability were the most influential predictors of chronic disease.

Conclusions

Automatically detected OCT biomarkers can predict CSC chronicity at initial presentation with good discriminatory performance. Quantitative markers of outer retinal integrity, fluid configuration, and RPE dysfunction may improve prognostication, facilitate patient counseling, and help identify individuals at increased risk of persistent CSC.

records.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: 3D Corneal and Retinal Bioprinting: Tissue Engineering Strategies, Translational Challenges, and Clinical Opportunities.
content.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with selected approaches entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

records.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Seeing in tandem: Cis and trans-regulation of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in zebrafish.
content.abstract: The molecular basis for vertebrate color vision is expression of spectrally-selective opsin-based photopigments within distinct cone photoreceptor populations. In several primates including humans, and in numerous fish species, genes encoding duplicated, spectrally-divergent cone opsin proteins may be positioned in tandem arrays. This article reviews studies of the regulation of differential expression of these duplicated cone opsin genes in humans and fish, with an emphasis on knowledge derived from the zebrafish model. In humans, the long wavelength-sensitive/medium wavelength-sensitive (LWS/MWS; red/green) tandemly-duplicated array underlies trichromatic color vision; mutations in this array cause altered color vision and retinal degenerations. A foundational model posited that regulation of human LWS vs. MWS opsin expression is stochastic, whereby an upstream enhancer associates randomly with promoters of the proximal or distal gene, and one of these associations becomes permanent. Discoveries of tandemly-duplicated cone opsin genes in teleost fish, including the versatile zebrafish model, led to their use to further pursue mechanisms of differential expression. The tandemly-duplicated zebrafish lws1 and lws2 genes (encoding red-sensing cone opsins) share a common ancestral gene with human LWS and MWS. Subsequent studies revealed that differential expression of these genes is regulated by the paracrine signal retinoic acid (RA) and the endocrine signal thyroid hormone (TH). Further investigations identified additional cone transcripts distinguishing zebrafish LWS1 vs. LWS2 cones, plasticity of cone opsin expression across the lifespan in response to TH, and a candidate receptor and cis-regulatory element. The findings warrant updates to the foundational model and further consideration of hypotheses for regulation of the human LWS vs. MWS genes.

records.title: Longitudinal Trajectories of 3-Dimensional Eye Shape and Pathological Sequelae in High Myopia.

content.title: Longitudinal Trajectories of 3-Dimensional Eye Shape and Pathological Sequelae in High Myopia.
content.abstract:
Importance

The highly myopic eye remodels in 3 dimensions, but the longitudinal trajectories of globe shape and their associations with sight-threatening outcomes remain poorly defined.

Objective

To characterize 15-year 3-dimensional (3D) remodeling trajectories of highly myopic globes and examine their associations with baseline features and ocular outcomes.

Design, setting, and participants

This 15-year 3D magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cohort substudy was nested within the Zhongshan High Myopia Cohort. Thirty participants (60 eyes) with bilateral high myopia (spherical equivalent refraction, -6.00 D or worse) randomly drawn from 95 participants imaged in September 2011 were rescanned in September 2025.

Exposures

Orbital 3D MRI reconstructions were classified into 6 globe-shape categories. Paired classifications, global enlargement, and staphyloma status defined 5 remodeling patterns: quiescence, proportional expansion, focal emergence, focal progression, and shape transition.

Main outcomes and measures

Distribution of remodeling patterns and their associations with myopic macular degeneration (MMD), myopic traction maculopathy (MTM), posterior staphyloma (PS), visual acuity, and visual field indices.

Results

Among the 30 included participants, the mean (SD) age was 37.30 (15.89) years, and 16 (53.3%) participants were women. The 60 eyes were classified as quiescent (21 [35.0%]), proportional expansion (12 [20.0%]), focal emergence (14 [23.3%]), focal progression (6 [10.0%]), or shape transition (7 [11.7%]). No deformed eye reverted to spheroidal. Pattern distribution was associated with baseline age and contour: 10 of 12 eyes (83.3%) of individuals younger than 20 years underwent proportional expansion, whereas 13 of 24 eyes (54.2%) of individuals aged 40 years and older followed focal progression or shape transition. Eyes with focal emergence had the largest best-corrected visual acuity decline (0.26 logMAR) and mean deviation worsening (-3.50 dB), and eyes with shape transition had the largest pattern standard deviation increasing (1.95 dB). At similar axial elongation, eyes developing focal deformation had higher frequencies of MMD progression (91.7%; 95% CI, 74.2-97.7 vs 58.8%; 95% CI, 36.0-78.4; P = .02), incident or progressive PS (91.7%; 95% CI, 74.2-97.7 vs 17.6%; 95% CI, 6.2-41.0; P < .001), and MTM (58.3%; 95% CI, 38.8-75.5 vs 11.8%; 95% CI, 3.3-34.3; P = .003).

Conclusions and relevance

Highly myopic globes followed age- and geometry-associated trajectories linked to outcomes beyond axial elongation. These 2-time-point findings potentially support 3D shape analysis as a candidate framework for individualized surveillance, pending prospective validation.

records.title: Ocular Changes in Human Spaceflight.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Ocular Changes in Human Spaceflight.
content.abstract: Spaceflight presents unique challenges to ocular health, with astronauts experiencing a range of visual disturbances in the setting of microgravity, radiation exposure, and other environmental factors. This review synthesizes knowledge about how spaceflight affects ocular anatomy and function. We outline the diagnostic and therapeutic limitations in microgravity, including constraints on imaging modalities, intracranial pressure measurement, and drug delivery. In addition, we examine common spaceflight-associated ocular pathologies, including spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome, corneal epithelial disruption, possible radiation-associated lens changes, and retinal or choroidal alterations. Drawing from evidence across human missions, terrestrial analogs, and experimental models, this review emphasizes the critical importance of vision to astronaut safety and mission success. Future directions include long-term ocular health monitoring, advancement of in-flight diagnostic capabilities, and multidisciplinary strategies to safeguard astronaut vision.

records.title: Retina Insurance Reimbursements of Pediatric Retina Patients in a Hospital versus Outpatient Surgical Setting.

content.title: Retina Insurance Reimbursements of Pediatric Retina Patients in a Hospital versus Outpatient Surgical Setting.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate reimbursement patterns for pediatric vitreoretinal procedures performed at a tertiary children's hospital versus an ambulatory surgery center (ASC).

Methods

A retrospective review was conducted of retinal procedures in pediatric patients performed between 1/2022 and 1/2025 at a tertiary children's hospital and an ambulatory surgery center in Texas. Self-pay visits and visits with zero billed charges were excluded. The primary outcome was total median reimbursement percentage based on physician-level services. Secondary outcomes included median reimbursement percentage by payer type, public insurer subgroup, surgical setting, and current procedural terminology (CPT) code. The proportion of visits with zero reimbursement was also evaluated.

Results

394 visits from 282 patients were analyzed, including 219 visits at the children's hospital and 175 at the ASC. Median reimbursement was 34.0% (representing 85% of the equivalent Medicare reimbursement rate). Public insurers reimbursed a higher median percentage than private insurers (35.1% vs. 26.5%, P=0.001). Reimbursement was lower at the hospital than the ASC (29.1% vs 36.3%, P<0.0001). 24.1% of visits received zero payment, occurring more frequently among privately insured than publicly insured visits (30.8% vs. 17.3%, P=0.003). Complex retinal detachment repair reimbursed less for private than public insurers (35.4% vs. 42.7%, P< 0.001).

Conclusion

Private insurers reimbursed lower than public insurers for pediatric vitreoretinal procedures, contrary to patterns commonly reported in adult retinal care. Procedures performed at a tertiary children's hospital resulted in lower reimbursements than those performed at an ASC. Frequent zero-payment encounters, particularly among private insurers, pose challenges that adversely affect the financial sustainability of pediatric retinal care.

records.title: Therapy with voretigene neparvovec. How to measure success?
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Therapy with voretigene neparvovec. How to measure success?
content.abstract: Retinal gene supplementation therapy such as the first approved one, voretigene neparvovec, delivers a functioning copy of the missing gene enabling the protein transcription in retinal cells and restore visual functions. After gene supplementation for the genetic defect, a complex network of functional regeneration is the consequence, whereas the extent is very individualized. Diagnostic and functional testings that have been used routinely by ophthalmologists so far to define the correct diagnosis, cannot be applied in the new context of defining small, sometimes subtle changes in visual functions. New view on retinal diagnostics is needed to understand this processes that define safety and efficacy of the treatment. Not only does vision have many aspects that must be addressed by specific evaluations and imaging techniques, but objective readouts of local retinal function for rods and cones separately have been an unmet need until recently. A reliable test-retest variability is necessary in rare diseases such as inherited retinal dystrophies, because statistics are often not applicable due to a low number of participants. Methods for a reliable individual evaluation of the therapy success are needed. In this manuscript we present an elaboration on retinal diagnostics combining psychophysics (eg. full-field stimulus threshold or dark adapted perimetry) as well as objective measures for local retinal function (eg. photopic and scotopic chromatic pupil campimetry) and retinal imaging for a meaningful workflow to apply in evaluation of the individual success in patients receiving gene therapy for photoreceptor diseases.

records.title: Myocilin misfolding and glaucoma: A 20-year update.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Myocilin misfolding and glaucoma: A 20-year update.
content.abstract: Mutations in the gene MYOC account for approximately 5% of cases of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG). MYOC encodes for the protein myocilin, a multimeric secreted glycoprotein composed of N-terminal coiled-coil (CC) and leucine zipper (LZ) domains that are connected via a disordered linker to a 30 kDa olfactomedin (OLF) domain. More than 90% of glaucoma-causing mutations are localized to the OLF domain. While myocilin is expressed in numerous tissues, mutant myocilin is only associated with disease in the anterior segment of the eye, in the trabecular meshwork. The prevailing pathogenic mechanism involves a gain of toxic function whereby mutant myocilin aggregates intracellularly instead of being secreted, which causes cell stress and an early timeline for TM cell death, elevated intraocular pressure, and subsequent glaucoma-associated retinal degeneration. In this review, we focus on the work our lab has conducted over the past ∼15 years to enhance our molecular understanding of myocilin-associated glaucoma, which includes details of the molecular structure and the nature of the aggregates formed by mutant myocilin. We conclude by discussing open questions, such as predicting phenotype from genotype alone, the elusive native function of myocilin, and translational directions enabled by our work.

records.title: The pre-Descemet's layer (Dua's layer, also known as the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer): Discovery, characterisation, clinical and surgical applications, and the controversy.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The pre-Descemet's layer (Dua's layer, also known as the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer): Discovery, characterisation, clinical and surgical applications, and the controversy.
content.abstract: The pre-Descemet's layer/Dua's layer, also termed the Dua-Fine layer and the pre-posterior limiting lamina layer, lies anterior to the Descemet's membrane in the cornea, is 10 μm (range 6-16) thick, made predominantly of type I and some type VI collagen with abundant elastin, more than any other layer of the cornea. It has high tensile strength (bursting pressure up to 700 mm of Hg), is impervious to air and almost acellular. At the periphery it demonstrates fenestrations and ramifies to become the core of the trabecular meshwork, with implications for intraocular pressure and glaucoma. It has been demonstrated in some species of animals. The layer has assumed considerable importance in anterior and posterior lamellar corneal transplant surgery by improving our understanding of the behaviour of corneal tissue during these procedures, improved techniques and made the surgery safer with better outcomes. It has led to the innovation of new surgical procedures namely, pre-Descemet's endothelial keratoplasty, suture management of acute hydrops, DALK-triple and Fogla's mini DALK. The discovery and knowledge of the layer has introduced paradigm shifts in our age old concepts of Descemet's membrane detachment, acute corneal hydrops in keratoconus and Descemetoceles, with impact on management approaches. It has been shown to contribute to the pathology and clinical signs observed in corneal infections and some corneal dystrophies. Early evidence suggests that it may have a role in the pathogenesis of keratoconus in relation to its elastin content. Its contribution to corneal biomechanics and glaucoma are subjects of current investigations.

records.title: Gene-independent therapeutic interventions to maintain and restore light sensitivity in degenerating photoreceptors.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Gene-independent therapeutic interventions to maintain and restore light sensitivity in degenerating photoreceptors.
content.abstract: Neurodegenerative retinal diseases are a prime cause of blindness in industrialized countries. In many cases, there are no therapeutic treatments, although they are essential to improve patients' quality of life. A set of disease-causing genes, which primarily affect photoreceptors, has already been identified and is of major interest for developing gene therapies. Nevertheless, depending on the nature and the state of the disease, gene-independent strategies are needed. Various strategies to halt disease progression or maintain function of the retina are under research. These therapeutic interventions include neuroprotection, direct reprogramming of affected photoreceptors, the application of non-coding RNAs, the generation of artificial photoreceptors by optogenetics and cell replacement strategies. During recent years, major breakthroughs have been made such as the first optogenetic application to a blind patient whose visual function partially recovered by targeting retinal ganglion cells. Also, RPE cell transplantation therapies are under clinical investigation and show great promise to improve visual function in blind patients. These cells are generated from human stem cells. Similar therapies for replacing photoreceptors are extensively tested in pre-clinical models. This marks just the start of promising new cures taking advantage of developments in the areas of genetic engineering, optogenetics, and stem-cell research. In this review, we present the recent therapeutic advances of gene-independent approaches that are currently under clinical evaluation. Our main focus is on photoreceptors as these sensory cells are highly vulnerable to degenerative diseases, and are crucial for light detection.

records.title: Challenges in the diagnosis and management of vitreoretinal lymphoma - Clinical and basic approaches.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Challenges in the diagnosis and management of vitreoretinal lymphoma - Clinical and basic approaches.
content.abstract: Vitreoretinal lymphoma (VRL) is a subtype of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and is sight- and life-threatening in the vast majority of patients. Lymphoma cells infiltrate the vitreous body and/or subretinal space and exhibit clinical signs of vitreous opacities and creamy white subretinal lesions. Although the intraocular signs can serve as clues to suspect VRL, they are nonspecific and may be misdiagnosed as uveitis. Histopathological evidence of malignant cells on vitreous biopsy, for instance, is the gold standard for diagnosis of VRL; however, cytological examination of the vitreous often results in a low success rate owing to the small quantity and poor quality of tissues and cells in the sample. Recent advancements in immunological, molecular, and gene analyses using intraocular samples have made it possible to accurately diagnose VRL. As for the management of VRL, local treatments with irradiation and/or intravitreal injections of anti-tumor agents (methotrexate or rituximab) are effective in suppressing intraocular VRL lesions. However, the effect of systemic chemotherapy, with or without brain irradiation, on preventing central nervous system involvements remains controversial. In this review article, we discuss the following concepts based on previous literature and our unpublished results: current ocular imaging examinations such as optical coherence tomography and fundus autofluorescence; immunological, molecular, and gene expression characterization of intraocular biopsies with special attention to flow cytometry; immunoglobulin gene rearrangement assays that use the polymerase chain reaction test; cytokine assays; gene mutations (MYD88, CD79B); and current local and systemic treatments of VRL.

records.title: The lens epithelium as a major determinant in the development, maintenance, and regeneration of the crystalline lens.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: The lens epithelium as a major determinant in the development, maintenance, and regeneration of the crystalline lens.
content.abstract: The crystalline lens is a transparent and refractive biconvex structure formed by lens epithelial cells (LECs) and lens fibers. Lens opacity, also known as cataracts, is the leading cause of blindness in the world. LECs are the principal cells of lens throughout human life, exhibiting different physiological properties and functions. During the embryonic stage, LECs proliferate and differentiate into lens fibers, which form the crystalline lens. Genetics and environment are vital factors that influence normal lens development. During maturation, LECs help maintain lens homeostasis through material transport, synthesis and metabolism as well as mitosis and proliferation. If disturbed, this will result in loss of lens transparency. After cataract surgery, the repair potential of LECs is activated and the structure and transparency of the regenerative tissue depends on postoperative microenvironment. This review summarizes recent research advances on the role of LECs in lens development, homeostasis, and regeneration, with a particular focus on the role of cholesterol synthesis (eg., lanosterol synthase) in lens development and homeostasis maintenance, and how the regenerative potential of LECs can be harnessed to develop surgical strategies and improve the outcomes of cataract surgery (Fig. 1). These new insights suggest that LECs are a major determinant of the physiological and pathological state of the lens. Further studies on their molecular biology will offer possibility to explore new approaches for cataract prevention and treatment.

records.title: Glaucoma Genetic Risk Scores in the Million Veteran Program.

content.title: Glaucoma Genetic Risk Scores in the Million Veteran Program.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a degenerative eye disease for which early treatment is critical to mitigate visual impairment and irreversible blindness. POAG-associated loci individually confer incremental risk. Genetic risk score(s) (GRS) could enable POAG risk stratification. Despite significantly higher POAG burden among individuals of African ancestry (AFR), GRS are limited in this population. A recent large-scale, multi-ancestry meta-analysis identified 127 POAG-associated loci and calculated cross-ancestry and ancestry-specific effect estimates, including in European ancestry (EUR) and AFR individuals. We assessed the utility of the 127-variant GRS for POAG risk stratification in EUR and AFR Veterans in the Million Veteran Program (MVP). We also explored the association between GRS and documented invasive glaucoma surgery (IGS).

Design

Cross-sectional study.

Participants

MVP Veterans with imputed genetic data, including 5830 POAG cases (445 with IGS documented in the electronic health record) and 64 476 controls.

Methods

We tested unweighted and weighted GRS of 127 published risk variants in EUR (3382 cases and 58 811 controls) and AFR (2448 cases and 5665 controls) Veterans in the MVP. Weighted GRS were calculated using effect estimates from the most recently published report of cross-ancestry and ancestry-specific meta-analyses. We also evaluated GRS in POAG cases with documented IGS.

Main outcome measures

Performance of 127-variant GRS in EUR and AFR Veterans for POAG risk stratification and association with documented IGS.

Results

GRS were significantly associated with POAG (P < 5 × 10-5) in both groups; a higher proportion of EUR compared with AFR were consistently categorized in the top GRS decile (21.9%-23.6% and 12.9%-14.5%, respectively). Only GRS weighted by ancestry-specific effect estimates were associated with IGS documentation in AFR cases; all GRS types were associated with IGS in EUR cases.

Conclusions

Varied performance of the GRS for POAG risk stratification and documented IGS association in EUR and AFR Veterans highlights (1) the complex risk architecture of POAG, (2) the importance of diverse representation in genomics studies that inform GRS construction and evaluation, and (3) the necessity of expanding diverse POAG-related genomic data so that GRS can equitably aid in screening individuals at high risk of POAG and who may require more aggressive treatment.

records.title: The Pattern of Retinal Ganglion Cell Loss in Wolfram Syndrome is Distinct From Mitochondrial Optic Neuropathies.

content.title: The Pattern of Retinal Ganglion Cell Loss in Wolfram Syndrome is Distinct From Mitochondrial Optic Neuropathies.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To describe the clinical phenotype of a cohort of patients with Wolfram syndrome (WS), focusing on the pattern of optic atrophy correlated with brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) measurements, as compared with patients with OPA1-related dominant optic atrophy (DOA).

Design

Retrospective, comparative cohort study.

Methods

We reviewed 25 patients with WS and 33 age-matched patients affected by OPA1-related DOA. Ophthalmologic, neurologic, endocrinologic, and MRI data from patients with WS were retrospectively retrieved. Ophthalmologic data were compared with data from patients with OPA1-related DOA and further analyzed for age dependency dividing patients in age quartiles. In a subgroup of patients with WS, we correlated the structural damage assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT) with brain MRI morphologic measurements. Visual acuity (VA), visual field mean defect (MD), retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL), and ganglion cell layer (GCL) thickness were assessed by OCT and MRI morphologic measurements of anterior and posterior visual pathways.

Results

Optic atrophy was present in 100% of patients with WS. VA, MD, and RNFL thickness loss were worse in patients with WS with a faster decline since early age as compared with patients with DOA, who displayed a more stable visual function over the years. Conversely, GCL sectors were overall thinner in patients with DOA since early age compared to patients with WS, in which GCL thickness started to decline later in life. The neuroradiologic subanalysis on 11 patients with WS exhibited bilateral thinning of the anterior optic pathway, especially the prechiasmatic optic nerves and optic tracts. Optic tract thinning was significantly correlated with GCL thickness but not with RNFL parameters.

Conclusions

Our results showed a generally more severe and diffuse degeneration of both anterior and posterior visual pathways in patients with WS, with fast deterioration of visual function and structural OCT parameters since early age. The pattern observed with OCT suggests that retinal ganglion cell axonal degeneration (ie, RNFL) precedes cellular body atrophy (ie, GCL) by about a decade. This differs substantially from DOA, in which a more stable visual function is evident with predominant early loss of GCL, indirectly supporting the lack of a primary mitochondrial dysfunction in patients with WS.

records.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the refractive predictive accuracy of the Moussa intraocular lens (IOL) formula compared with Kane, EVO, PEARL-DGS, K6, Hoffer-QST, and Barrett Universal II (BUII).

Setting

Birmingham Midland Eye Centre (Birmingham), Manchester Royal Eye Hospital and Newmedica (Manchester), UK.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective, consecutive, nonrandomized observational case series (September 2022-June 2025).

Methods

Included were one eye per patient undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Preoperative biometry used the IOLMaster 700, Lenstar LS900, or Pentacam AXL Wave. Lens-constants were optimized to zero mean prediction error (PE) for each formula and lens-biometer combination. Primary outcome was mean absolute error (MAE), evaluated using heteroscedastic studentized bootstrap analysis (2000 iterations; Holm correction). Secondary outcomes included median absolute error, root-mean-square error, standard deviation of PE, and proportions of eyes within ±0.25diopter (D) and ±0.50D.

Results

Included were 2550 patients (2550 eyes; mean age 74.0±10.0 years; 1068 male patients [41.9%]). Moussa produced a lower MAE (0.348 D) than Kane (0.359D), EVO (0.363D), PEARL-DGS (0.367D), K6 (0.367D), Hoffer-QST (0.377D), and BUII (0.379D; all p<.001). In short eyes (≤22.0mm), Moussa (0.412D) demonstrated lower error than K6 (p<.001), BUII (p<.001), Hoffer-QST (p=.008), EVO (p=.008), PEARL-DGS (p=.014), and Kane (p=.039). In long eyes (≥26.0 mm), Moussa (0.342 D) had lower error than Kane, BUII, Hoffer-QST (all p<.001), and K6 (p=.045), but not EVO (p=.068) or PEARL-DGS (p=.202).

Conclusions

The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted validation.

records.title: Accuracy of six contemporary toric formulas: analysis of 6753 eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Accuracy of six contemporary toric formulas: analysis of 6753 eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the predictive accuracy of 4 toric intraocular lens (IOL) formulas (Barrett, EVO, Hoffer QST, and Kane) integrated in the ESCRS calculator. Barrett and EVO were tested with measured (Barrett M and EVO M) and predicted (Barrett P and EVO P) posterior corneal curvature.

Setting

Multiple surgical centers in the United States.

Design

Retrospective database study.

Methods

6753 eyes implanted with nontoric IOLs were analyzed. Preoperative biometry, including posterior corneal curvature, was obtained using the IOLMaster 700. Predicted residual astigmatism was calculated through the proprietary websites of the 4 toric formulas integrated into the ESCRS IOL power calculator. Primary endpoints were the mean vector magnitude error and proportions of eyes with vector magnitude prediction errors ≤0.50 diopters (D).

Results

Kane demonstrated the lowest mean vector magnitude prediction error (0.537 D), significantly lower than EVO P (0.561 D), EVO M (0.57 D), Barrett M (0.579 D), Barrett P (0.583 D), and Hoffer QST (0.622 D) (all P < .001). This result was consistent in with-the-rule, against-the-rule, and oblique subgroups. Kane also achieved the highest proportion of eyes with prediction error ≤0.50 D ( P < .001). For all formulas, centroid values were significantly different from zero. The Kane formula showed the lowest total variances, significantly lower than all other formulas ( P < .001).

Conclusions

The Kane formula showed statistically superior predictive accuracy with the lowest errors and variances and the highest proportion of eyes within 0.50 D. However, differences among formulas were small, and their clinical relevance for toric IOL outcomes remains uncertain.

records.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Improving effective lens position prediction for secondary intraocular lens implantation in pediatric aphakic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To improve the accuracy of refractive prediction for pediatric secondary sulcus intraocular lens (IOL) implantation by optimizing the effective lens position (ELP) prediction within the SRK/T formula.

Setting

Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Guangzhou, China.

Design

Retrospective consecutive case-series.

Methods

The value of sulcus-ELP was identified by linear regression formula with utilizing back-calculated ELP. The obtained sulcus-ELP was subsequently incorporated into the original SRK/T formula, then creating the sulcus-SRK/T formula. The prediction accuracy of sulcus-SRK/T formula was compared with six formulas. Main outcome measures included prediction error (PE), mean error (ME), median absolute error (MedAE), and the percentage of eyes with prediction error within ±0.50 diopters (D) and ±1.00 D.

Results

This study included 86 pediatric patients (131 eyes) who underwent secondary ciliary sulcus IOL implantation. With the modified formula, the percentages of eyes achieving the prediction error (PE) within ±0.50 D and ±1.00 D were 25.6% and 53.9%, respectively, significantly higher than those of other formulas. The mean error (ME) of the modified formula was 0.46±1.39 D, and the modified formula showed lower median absolute error (MedAE) (0.95 D, P < .05) than other formulas.

Conclusions

By optimizing ELP prediction of the SRK/T formula, the prediction accuracy of pediatric secondary sulcus IOL implantation has been improved. The sulcus-SRK/T formula is a worthwhile choice and requires further external validation to confirm its effectiveness.

records.title: Incidence of secondary intraocular lens implantation in school-aged children left aphakic to age 4.5 years in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Incidence of secondary intraocular lens implantation in school-aged children left aphakic to age 4.5 years in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine the incidence of secondary intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in a cohort of children randomized to aphakia after unilateral congenital cataract surgery.

Setting

12 clinical sites in the United States.

Design

Randomized clinical trial. Data regarding secondary IOL implantation were collected retrospectively when patients were age 10.5 years.

Methods

We calculated the cumulative incidence of secondary IOL implantation in participants in the Infant Aphakia Treatment Study who were randomized to aphakia to age 4.5 years and were followed at age 10.5 years.

Results

22 (43%, 95% CI, 29%-58%) of the 51 participants left aphakic to age 4.5 years who had better than light perception vision at age 4.5 years received a secondary IOL by age 10.5. More than half (59%) of these were implanted by age 6 (median 64.5 months, interquartile range 60-80). Secondary IOLs were implanted in children with good visual acuity (≤20/40), as well as those with poor visual outcomes (≥20/200) (39% and 44%, respectively). Children who received a secondary IOL did not report less contact lens wear than those remaining aphakic (average of 94% of waking hours vs 90%, respectively). However, the proportion of children receiving a secondary IOL varied substantially by study center.

Conclusions

Many children with unilateral congenital cataract who are initially left aphakic remain aphakic throughout the elementary school years. Practice patterns and family preference seem to be important drivers of the decision to implant a secondary IOL in these children.

records.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the demographic, ocular, systemic, and histopathologic features of patients undergoing surgery for late intraocular lens (IOL) instability with clinically suspected dead bag syndrome (DBS).

Setting

Private ophthalmology practice and tertiary ophthalmic pathology laboratory.

Design

Single-center consecutive case series with prospective tissue collection and retrospective chart review.

Methods

Capsular bag remnants were explanted during secondary IOL surgery and submitted for histopathologic examination. Demographic, ocular, and systemic characteristics were obtained from the medical record. Lens epithelial cell (LEC) status was graded as 0 = absent; 1 = rare residual LECs; 2 = focal identifiable LEC segments. Specimens were assessed for capsular splitting/schisis, cortical material, and anterior capsular fibrous metaplasia. Exploratory clinical comparisons were performed between LEC grade 0 and LEC grade 1-2 subgroups.

Results

Thirty-one eyes from 26 patients underwent secondary IOL surgery for late IOL subluxation or dislocation with clinical suspicion of DBS, including 27 with histopathologic evaluation. Mean age at secondary surgery was 70.5 ± 10.5 years and 80.7% patients were male. Median time from cataract surgery to presentation was 13.0 years (IQR 9.0-16.5). Axial myopia was present in 6/31 eyes (19.4%). Atopy was documented in 9/31 (29.0%), prior radiation or chemotherapy exposure in 8/31 (25.8%), autoimmune disease in 10/31 (32.3%), and ACE inhibitor or ARB use in 14/31 (45.2%). Complete LEC absence (grade 0) was present in 8/27 (29.6%), while 19/27 (70.4%) demonstrated residual LECs and/or cortical material (grades 1-2). Spontaneous posterior capsular rupture was documented in 15/31 (48.4%) cases and in 15/27 (55.6%) histopathology-confirmed cases. Atopy was more frequent in LEC grade 0 than among LEC grade 1-2 eyes (37.5% vs 15.8%; P = 0.32), though this did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusions

DBS represents a histopathologically definable spectrum of capsular degeneration characterized by LEC depletion and capsular splitting with structural failure leading to late IOL instability. Nearly half of confirmed cases presented without clinically evident spontaneous posterior capsular rupture, suggesting that rupture is not required for DBS diagnosis.

records.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.

Setting

10 European study centers.

Design

Prospective observational multicenter study.

Methods

Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.

Results

In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.

records.title: Dilated Pupil Vertical-to-Horizontal Ratio as a Predictor of Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Dilated Pupil Vertical-to-Horizontal Ratio as a Predictor of Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate whether intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) can be predicted from pupil morphology, including vertical pupil elongation and pupillary diameter.

Setting

Shiga University of Medical Science Hospital, Shiga, Japan.

Design

Retrospective observational study.

Methods

Patients who underwent standalone phacoemulsification cataract surgery between November 2022 and April 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. In bilateral cases, only the first operated eye was included. Eyes with prior ocular surgery or conditions affecting pupil morphology were excluded. Surgical videos were reviewed to assess pupil morphology parameters, including the pupil vertical-to-horizontal ratio (PVHR) and the composite pupil-to-corneal diameter ratio (CPCDR) at the beginning of surgery, and to evaluate IFIS incidence. IFIS incidence was treated as the outcome variable. Explanatory variables comprised age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, α1-adrenergic antagonist use, and pupil morphology parameters. Associations were evaluated using logistic regression.

Results

A total of 263 patients (263 eyes) were included, of which 23 eyes (8.7%) developed IFIS. PVHR was significantly higher in eyes with vs without IFIS (median: 1.06 vs 1.03; p < 0.001), while CPCDR was significantly lower (0.56 vs 0.70; p < 0.001). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, PVHR (odds ratio: 4.06; p = 0.0005) and CPCDR (odds ratio: 0.43; p < 0.0001) were independently associated with IFIS.

Conclusions

Vertical pupil elongation and poor dilation after pharmacologic mydriasis were independently associated with IFIS. Assessment of pupil shape, in addition to pupil size, may improve preoperative identification of eyes at risk for IFIS.

records.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Ray-Tracing Aberrometry and the Dysfunctional Lens Index for Objective Assessment of Posterior Capsular Opacification.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dysfunctional lens index (DLI), higher-order aberrations (HOA), and modulation transfer function (MTF) from ray-tracing aberrometry as objective markers of posterior capsular opacification (PCO) and treatment response.

Setting

Two tertiary ophthalmology centers, Istanbul, Turkey.

Design

Prospective interventional study with a clear-capsule pseudophakic control group.

Methods

Eyes with visually significant PCO after uncomplicated phacoemulsification with monofocal IOL implantation underwent ray-tracing aberrometry and 4 weeks after Nd:YAG capsulotomy; one eye per patient was analysed. CDVA, DLI, total and internal HOA root mean square (RMS), Zernike components, and MTF at 5-30 cycles/degree (cpd) were compared with clear-capsule control eyes with the same IOL.

Results

Thirty-one eyes of 31 patients (mean age 66.7 years; 21 female) and 28 control eyes were included. All parameters improved after capsulotomy (all P<.001): CDVA from 0.52 to 0.10 logMAR, DLI from 3.10 to 7.20, internal HOA RMS by 66.9%. Internal coma and trefoil decreased, whereas spherical aberration was unchanged (negative control). MTF improved at all six spatial frequencies. Pre-operatively, PCO eyes were degraded relative to controls (DLI 3.35 vs 7.67; P<.001); post-operatively they matched controls (7.23 vs 7.67; P=.44). DLI correlated with internal HOA (r=-0.947) and MTF (r=+0.842) but not CDVA (r=-0.051).

Conclusions

Ray-tracing aberrometry offers an objective view of PCO-induced optical degradation. Because the DLI tracks internal aberrations and MTF yet remains independent of high-contrast acuity, it captures impairment that CDVA alone overlooks, and returns to clear-capsule levels after capsulotomy. The DLI thus serves as a useful adjunctive marker for gauging PCO-related degradation and monitoring treatment response.

records.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effect of dry eye disease (DED) and ocular surface treatment on the agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace in patients with age-related cataract.

Setting

Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai, China.

Design

Prospective, single-center study.

Methods

A total of 313 eyes of patients with age-related cataract were included. Eyes with DED received 0.3% sodium hyaluronate eye drops for 2 weeks and were re-examined after treatment. Corneal astigmatism measurements were obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace before pupil dilation. The main parameters included keratometric corneal astigmatism, total corneal astigmatism, and their vector components. Interdevice agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, and test-retest repeatability was evaluated using within-subject standard deviation, test-retest repeatability, and intraclass correlation coefficients.

Results

Compared with the control group, eyes at DED baseline showed wider limits of agreement and poorer TRT for both scalar astigmatism parameters and vector components. After ocular surface treatment, LoA width decreased by 50.5%-62.5% for KCA and 19.9%-29.0% for TCA across the three device comparisons. KCA repeatability improved significantly after treatment for IOLMaster 700 and iTrace, whereas significant improvement in TCA repeatability was observed only for IOLMaster 700. Device- and parameter-specific differences persisted after treatment.

Conclusions

DED was associated with reduced agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace. Short-term ocular surface treatment was associated with improved measurement stability.

records.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
content.abstract: Posterior chamber phakic intraocular lenses have a strong short-to-medium-term safety profile on the modern central-port platform, and a 2025 US Food and Drug Administration expansion of the indicated age range for a central-port phakic IOL to 21 to 60 years widens the eligible population. These lenses are to remain in the eye for decades, yet the field has defined what to monitor without building the infrastructure to deliver that monitoring reliably as patients age, change providers, and relocate. Existing guidance specifies endothelial and vault thresholds but does not address who monitors after the implanting surgeon, how baseline and longitudinal data transfer, or how late events are learned across practices. We propose three measures: upgrading the implant identification card into a longitudinal, portable surveillance record; a risk-stratified, age-informed surveillance framework developed through multisociety consensus; and a prospective implant registry with a defined minimum dataset. The device's clinical maturation now requires a parallel evolution in its care model.

records.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term visual, refractive, and patient-reported satisfaction of epithelial photorefractive keratectomy (ePRK) combined with corneal cross-linking (CXL) - the Tel-Aviv Protocol - in patients with progressive keratoconus.

Setting

Care-Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel.

Design

Retrospective, single-center case series.

Methods

Consecutive patients with progressive keratoconus who underwent ePRK-CXL were included. Preoperative and last-available postoperative pachymetry, keratometry (Kmean, Kmin, Kmax), spherical equivalent (SEQ), manifest refraction, uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), and corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) were recorded; safety and efficacy indices were calculated. Patient-reported outcomes regarding spectacle/contact lens dependence, satisfaction, and visual symptoms were assessed with a structured questionnaire.

Results

Fifty eyes of 38 patients (mean age 25.9±6.8 years) were followed for a mean of 2,910±605 days (∼8 years; range 5-12). UDVA improved from 1.04±0.70 to 0.36±0.37 logMAR and CDVA from 0.23±0.16 to 0.11±0.10 logMAR (both P < 0.001); safety and efficacy indices were 1.42±0.55 and 0.93±0.51. K-max decreased from 47.51±2.96 to 45.95±2.99 D and SEQ from -2.42±2.29 to -0.82±1.57 D (both P < 0.001). Pachymetry decreased from 448.65±38.95 to 418.93±55.77 μm. Overall satisfaction was high (81.6% satisfied/very satisfied), 76.3% reported subjective visual improvement, 52.6% achieved spectacle independence, and 92.1% required no contact lenses. No progression was observed in the examined eyes.

Conclusions

At a mean follow-up of ∼8 years, the Tel-Aviv Protocol provided durable visual and refractive improvement, stabilized keratometry without progression, and yielded high patient satisfaction with low symptom burden. These results support ePRK-CXL as a tissue-sparing option for progressive keratoconus.

records.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.

content.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.
content.abstract:
Importance

US ophthalmology residency programs are divided between traditional resident clinic-based models with a separate faculty practice, and universal practice-based models. Little data exist comparing these educational models.

Objective

To evaluate the association of changing a traditional resident clinic training model to a universal practice plus urgent eye clinic-based residency training model with sociodemographic disparities and resident education.

Design, setting, and participants

This was a cross-sectional study conducted at a US academic medical center. All patients presenting to the University of Rochester Flaum Eye Institute between the period July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, and the period July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, were divided into 4 cohorts for retrospective analysis as follows: resident clinic 2017-2019, faculty practice 2017-2019, urgent eye clinic 2022-2024, and universal practice 2022-2024.

Exposures

The resident clinic was transitioned to urgent eye clinic in July 2022. All former patients from resident clinic were reassigned to the new universal practice.

Main outcomes and measures

Patient cohorts were compared regarding insurance payor(s) and self-identified race. Level of disease acuity in resident clinic and urgent eye clinic were compared. Graduating resident procedural volumes were compared.

Results

Participants were divided into the following 4 cohorts: resident clinic 2017-2019 (6819 patients), faculty practice 2017-2019 (61 847 patients), urgent eye clinic 2022-2024 (5124 patients), and universal practice 2022-2024 (79 001 patients), for a total of 118 459 patients (mean [SD] age, 47 [25] years; 65 186 female [55%]). Pretransition, compared with faculty practice patients, greater proportions of resident clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (62.1% vs 19.4%; difference, 32.0%; 95% CI, 30.9%-33.1%; P < .001) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native (ie, American Indian or Alaska Native), or other (51.9% vs 23.6%; difference, 28.3%; 95% CI, 27.1%-29.5%; P < .001). Posttransition, compared with universal practice patients, similar proportions of urgent eye clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (26.8% vs 27.8%; difference, 0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to 1.6%; P = .42) and identified as Asian, Black or African American, multiracial, native, or other (29.6% vs 26.8%; difference, 2.8%; 95% CI, 1.5%-4.1%; P < .001). A greater proportion of urgent eye clinic patients presented with high-acuity disease (37.6%) compared with resident clinic patients (20.9%; difference, 16.7%; 95% CI, 15.0%-18.4%; P < .001). Median graduating resident primary cataract surgery volume increased from 148 to 228 cases (difference, 80; 95% CI, 49 to 122; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance

Results of this cross-sectionals study show that transforming resident clinic into urgent eye clinic was associated with reduced sociodemographic disparities, enhanced resident exposure to high-acuity disease, and increased resident procedural experience. These results suggest that changes in resident clinic structure may improve both health equity and resident education.

records.title: Diabetes Severity in Cornea Donors and 1-Year Outcomes in Recipients in the Diabetes Endothelial Keratoplasty Study: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.

content.title: Diabetes Severity in Cornea Donors and 1-Year Outcomes in Recipients in the Diabetes Endothelial Keratoplasty Study: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial.
content.abstract:
Importance

The effect of cornea donor diabetes severity on graft success, endothelial cell density (ECD), and morphometry after Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) is not known.

Objective

To determine whether graft success, corneal endothelial cell loss (ECL), and morphometric changes 1 year after DMEK are associated with cornea donor diabetes severity measured by severity score, donor's postmortem level of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and postmortem advanced glycation end products (AGEs) or advanced oxidation end products (AOPs).

Design, setting, and participants

This was a secondary analysis of a multicenter, double-masked, randomized clinical trial at 28 clinical sites (46 surgeons) and 13 eye banks in the US among individuals undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of donors. Data analysis was conducted from September 1, 2025, through April 30, 2026.

Intervention

DMEK performed with a cornea from a donor without or with diabetes, assigned using a minimization procedure (comparable to randomization) to achieve an approximate 2:1 distribution, respectively.

Main outcomes and measures

Graft success, ECL, coefficient of variation (CV) of cell area, and percentage of hexagonal cells (HEX) at 1 year from eye bank and postoperative specular central endothelial images.

Results

A total of 1097 individuals (1421 study eyes; median [IQR] age, 71 [66-76] years; 631 [57.5%] female) undergoing low- to moderate-risk DMEK (1044 [95.2%] for Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy) were included. AGE and AOP measurements were collected from a subset of 472 donors (542 study donor corneas). Among 968 eyes with a postmortem donor HbA1c level lower than 6.5%, the 1-year graft success rate was 97.1% (95% CI, 95.4%-98.4%), compared with 97.4% (95% CI, 93.9%-100.0%), 93.0% (95% CI, 83.3%-98.8%), and 95.8% (95% CI, 87.3%-100.0%) among eyes with a donor HbA1c level of 6.5% to less than 7.5% (n = 194), 7.5% to less than 9.0% (n = 86), and 9.0% or higher (n = 48), respectively (P = .72). There was no significant difference in mean ECD across donor HbA1c groups. Donor diabetes severity measured with severity score, donor HbA1c level, and AGE and AOP metrics was not associated with 1-year graft failure, ECD, CV in cell area, or HEX percentage.

Conclusions and relevance

This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial found that ECL and morphometry 1 year after DMEK were not affected by cornea donor diabetes severity. Comparable 1-year graft success, ECL, and cell morphometrics with tissue from donors with and without diabetes, regardless of the diabetes severity biomarker values observed, support the use of corneas from donors with diabetes for endothelial keratoplasty procedures without additional preoperative testing or risk stratification based on the diabetes status of the cornea donor.

Trial registration

ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05134480.

records.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.

content.title: Validation of the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS): Correlations with Clinical, Imaging, and Symptom Outcomes in Cystinosis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To prospectively validate the University of California, Irvine Corneal Cystine Crystal Score (UCI CCCS), a standardized slit-lamp grading tool, by evaluating associations with objective corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and visual acuity in a real-world cystinosis cohort.

Design

Prospective observational cross-sectional study.

Participants

Seventy patients (140 eyes) with confirmed cystinosis were examined at the 2024-2025 Cystinosis Research Foundation Day of Hope Clinics.

Methods

All eyes underwent live slit-lamp UCI CCCS grading (0-5). Pentacam Scheimpflug densitometry was obtained in 68 eyes. Two ophthalmologists independently graded patients during the 2025 clinic to assess inter-rater reliability. Patient-reported symptoms, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and topical cysteamine treatment data were collected. Linear mixed-effects models accounting for within-patient correlation were used for densitometry and BCVA analyses. Symptom associations were evaluated at the patient level using Kendall's tau-b.

Main outcome measures

Inter-rater reliability of UCI CCCS; associations with corneal densitometry, patient-reported symptoms, and BCVA.

Results

Inter-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.995; 95% CI, 0.992-0.996). Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated significant associations between UCI CCCS grade and central (p = 0.0016) and anterior corneal densitometry (p = 0.0011) after accounting for within-patient correlation between fellow eyes. Higher UCI CCCS grades were significantly associated with greater photophobia (τ = 0.397, p < 0.0001), foreign-body sensation (τ = 0.295, p = 0.0047), and ocular dryness (τ = 0.405, p = 0.0001). No statistically significant association was observed between UCI CCCS grade and BCVA after accounting for within-patient correlation (p = 0.4389). No significant differences in UCI CCCS or corneal densitometry were observed across topical cysteamine treatment groups.

Conclusion

The UCI CCCS is a highly reproducible, clinically practical grading tool associated with objective corneal densitometry and patient-reported symptom burden, while BCVA was not significantly associated with UCI CCCS grade. Longitudinal studies are needed to evaluate treatment responsiveness and prognostic value.

records.title: Subbasal Nerve Plexus Alterations Following Ocular Proton Therapy in Uveal Melanoma Assessed by Corneal Confocal Microscopy.

content.title: Subbasal Nerve Plexus Alterations Following Ocular Proton Therapy in Uveal Melanoma Assessed by Corneal Confocal Microscopy.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate longitudinal changes in the subbasal nerve plexus (SNP) after ocular proton therapy (OPT) in eyes with uveal melanoma and associated changes in corneal sensitivity, cell density, and patient-reported outcomes.

Design

Prospective clinical cohort study.

Subjects

Fifty-eight patients (58 eyes) with uveal melanoma were enrolled; 54 had evaluable baseline corneal confocal microscopy images, and 40 formed the longitudinal analysis cohort. Follow-up data were available for 30 patients at 3 months and 27 patients at 12 months.

Methods

Corneal confocal microscopy was used to assess SNP parameters and cell density. Corneal sensitivity was measured with a Cochet-Bonnet aesthesiometer. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed using the German Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) and selected domains from the German version of the NEI VFQ-25. Examinations were performed before OPT and at 3 and 12 months after OPT.

Main outcome measures

Primary outcome measures were changes in corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD), corneal nerve branch density (CNBD), and corneal nerve fiber length (CNFL). Secondary outcome measures included corneal nerve fiber tortuosity (CNFT), cell density, corneal sensitivity, OSDI, and selected NEI VFQ-25 domains.

Results

CNFD decreased from 18.2 to 11.4 (3 months) and 12.7 no./mm² (12 months) (P = .002 and .001). CNBD decreased from 23.9 to 13.5 and 15.8 no./mm² (P = .012 and .040), and CNFL from 11.0 to 6.2 and 7.3 mm/mm² (both P < .001). Nerve loss was associated with treatment-related exposure, particularly the clinical target volume. CNFT decreased at 3 months (P = .018) and approached baseline at 12 months (P = .28). Corneal sensitivity did not change significantly. OSDI increased at 12 months (P = .049). After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, the 3-month CNFT, 12-month OSDI, and 12-month cell density changes were no longer significant. Among NEI VFQ-25 domains, only peripheral vision declined (84 to 68; P = .006).

Conclusions

OPT was associated with marked reduction of SNP parameters, with only partial recovery by 12 months. Greater nerve loss was associated with larger treatment volumes and greater corneal irradiation. Cell density and corneal sensitivity remained unchanged, whereas patient-reported outcomes did not consistently reflect structural denervation.

records.title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis: Outcomes After Descemet Membrane Endothelial Keratoplasty Versus Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty.

content.title: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis: Outcomes After Descemet Membrane Endothelial Keratoplasty Versus Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the efficacy and safety of ultrathin Descemet stripping (automated) endothelial keratoplasty (UT-DS(A)EK) versus Descemet membrane endothelial keratoplasty (DMEK) for the treatment of Fuchs endothelial dystrophy (FED) and bullous keratopathy (BK).

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

Literature containing DMEK and UT-DSAEK were searched in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, PubMed, EMBASE, LILACS, and through manual reference searching. Studies were included that measured the outcome of interventions-including best corrected visual acuity (BCVA), endothelial cell density (ECD), and postoperative complications, especially graft detachment with the need of re-bubbling, graft rejection, graft failure, and postoperative elevated intraocular pressure (IOP)-in patients with FED and BK. Included outcomes were pooled as standardized mean differences (SMD) or risk ratios (RR) using random effects models. Inter-study heterogeneity was assessed using the Q-test and I2 statistic.

Results

Seven (of 163) studies met all the inclusion and exclusion criteria. Meta-analysis showed a significantly better BCVA 12 months postoperatively, but an increased re-bubbling rate in eyes after DMEK compared with eyes after UT-DS(A)EK (BCVA: SMD = 0.50 [95% CI 0.27-0.74] and re-bubbling rate: RR = 0.33 [95% CI 0.16-0.67]). All other parameters did not differ significantly between both interventions, although estimates were imprecise (graft failure: RR = 0.65 [95% CI 0.18-2.30], graft rejection: RR = 1.40 [95% CI 0.27-7.30], and postoperative intraocular pressure elevation: RR = 1.14 [95% CI 0.60-2.18]). Postoperative SMDs of ECD could not be evaluated due to significant heterogeneity between studies.

Conclusions

Although the improvement in BCVA was higher after UT-DS(A)EK than after conventional DS(A)EK, the BCVA after DMEK was still superior. The complication rates were comparable for both procedures, except for the higher rate of re-bubbling after DMEK.

records.title: Efficacy of Thin and Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty and Influence of Graft Thickness on Postoperative Outcomes: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy of Thin and Ultrathin Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty and Influence of Graft Thickness on Postoperative Outcomes: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of thin and ultrathin Descemet stripping automated endothelial keratoplasty (T-DSAEK and UT-DSAEK, with graft thickness <130 and <100 µm, respectively), depending on graft thickness.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Method

PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ScienceDirect databases were searched until October 1, 2021. We computed random-effect meta-analysis on postoperative outcomes of T/UT-DSAEK, stratified by graft thickness (<80 μm, 80-100 μm, and 100-130 μm). The main postoperative outcome was visual acuity (logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution [logMAR]). Secondary outcomes were pachymetry (μm), endothelial cell count (cell/mm2), spherical equivalent (diopter [D]), rebubbling rate (%), and rejection rate (%). Meta-regressions compared postoperative outcomes depending on graft thickness and search for putative confusion factors.

Results

We included 47 articles for a total of 2141 eyes of 2040 patients. T/UT-DSAEK globally improved visual acuity (effect size = -0.38 logMAR [95% confidence interval {CI} -0.46 to -0.30 logMAR]), without difference depending on graft thickness. Overall, pachymetry improved (-60.6 µm [95% CI -101 to -19.7 µm]), endothelial cell count decreased (-1039 cells/mm2 [95% CI -1209 to -868 cells/mm2), spherical equivalent resulted in a hyperopic shift (0.74 D [95% CI -0.50 to 1.97 D), the graft rejection rate was 0.2% (95% CI -0.1% to 0.4%), and the rebubbling rate was 8.7% (95% CI 6.8%-10.5%). Grafts >100 μm induced a hyperopic shift. Metaregressions did not demonstrate differences between the 3 groups (<80 μm, 80-100 μm, or 100-130 μm) in any outcomes.

Conclusion

All T/UT-DSAEK thickness groups provided similar visual acuity, pachymetry, endothelial cell count, rejection rate, and rebubbling rate regardless of graft thickness. A hyperopic shift was induced by grafts >100 μm.

records.title: Glands of Moll: history, current knowledge and their role in ocular surface homeostasis and disease.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Glands of Moll: history, current knowledge and their role in ocular surface homeostasis and disease.
content.abstract: Over the last 20 years, research into the Meibomian glands of the eyelids has increased exponentially and is now widely recognized as a field of research.
